questions.question: Explain the nominal/balance-sheet sorting and the meaning carried by the statement's heading.
questions.expected_answer: Nominal accounts (incomes and expenses) measure the year's flows and belong to the Statement of Comprehensive Income; balance sheet accounts (assets, liabilities, capital) measure position at a moment and belong to the Statement of Financial Position. The heading 'for the year ended 30 June' signals a period of accumulated flows, in contrast to 'at 30 June' which signals a moment's position — the prepositions FOR and AT encode the two kinds of account, and an incomplete heading loses marks.

questions.question: Build the statement's three layers with Zanele's figures, naming each subtotal.
questions.expected_answer: Trading layer: Sales R60 000 (R61 500 less R1 500 debtors allowances) minus Cost of Sales R40 000 gives GROSS PROFIT R20 000. Operating layer: plus other operating income (Rent Income R7 200) gives gross operating income R27 200; minus operating expenses (Salaries and Wages R7 800, Water and Electricity R2 940, Insurance R600, Stationery R450, Bank Charges R420, Trading Stock Deficit R190, Depreciation R2 800 — total R15 200) gives OPERATING PROFIT R12 000. Financing layer: plus interest income (none) minus interest expense R1 500 gives NET PROFIT FOR THE YEAR R10 500.

questions.question: Show the workings convention on three adjusted lines and explain the two placement rules the markers watch.
questions.expected_answer: Workings sit in brackets beside the line: Water and Electricity R2 940 (2 640 + 300 owing); Insurance R600 (1 800 − 1 200 prepaid); Rent Income R7 200 (6 600 + 600 accrued) — so the marker can award the route even if the final figure slips. Placement rules: the trading stock deficit is an operating expense (a surplus would join other operating income), and interest in both directions stays out of the operating block — operating profit must measure the operations alone, with financing framing it from below.
